title.rendered: New in store – Argyreia Nervosa

content.rendered:
Argyreia Nervosa, also known as Hawaiian Baby Woodrose, is a fascinating plant with a rich history. This perennial vine originates from the Indian subcontinent and is admired for its heart-shaped leaves and bright purple flowers.

Argyreia Nervosa seeds contain LSA, a natural compound with psychoactive properties. This makes the plant popular among those interested in natural psychedelics and traditional medicine.

We are excited to introduce new products containing Argyreia Nervosa in our store. These include seeds and other related products for enthusiasts and gardeners alike.

Whether you are a botanist or a hobbyist, Argyreia Nervosa offers both ornamental beauty and practical uses. Explore the potential of this unique plant and discover its many benefits.

What is Argyreia Nervosa (Hawaiian Rose)?

Argyreia Nervosa, or Hawaiian Rose, is an exotic plant with fascinating properties. Native to the Indian subcontinent, this climbing plant is prized for its ornamental and therapeutic properties.

Key Features:

  • Large, heart-shaped leaves – create a dense, green canopy.
  • Flowers – striking purple blooms attract attention and add vibrancy to any garden.
  • Growing environment – suitable for tropical and subtropical climates.

Argyreia Nervosa seeds contain LSA, which increases interest in this plant among those seeking natural alternatives to synthetic psychedelics. These seeds are known for their psychoactive properties, which make them sought after for specific ethnobotanical applications.

The plant is not only for shamanic practices, but also for ordinary gardeners who like to add a touch of the exotic to their gardens. Argyreia Nervosa is in many ways a versatile plant that deserves attention for its many uses.

History and traditional use

Argyreia Nervosa has a rich history in various cultures, where it has been used for centuries for its medicinal properties. It is known for its use in traditional Ayurvedic medicine, where it played an important role in the treatment of various diseases.

In traditional cultures, the plant was used not only for medicinal purposes, but also in rituals and spiritual practices. Argyreia Nervosa seeds were valued for their ability to induce altered states of consciousness, which was used in shamanic ceremonies.

Traditional uses of Argyreia Nervosa include:

  • Treatment of inflammation and pain
  • Support for mental and spiritual health
  • Use in natural and spiritual rituals

This history makes Argyreia Nervosa a fascinating example of the interconnection between nature and culture, where the plant bridges the gap between healing and spirituality.

LSA in Argyreia Nervosa Seeds: Effects and Safety

Argyreia Nervosa seeds contain LSA (lysergic acid amide), a natural compound known for its psychedelic properties. This substance affects the mind, often inducing altered states of consciousness that may include visual and emotional changes.

The psychoactive effects of LSA are similar to those of LSD, although less intense. As a result, the seeds are often used as a natural alternative to synthetic psychedelics, making them an attractive option for many users.

The effects of LSA may include:

  • Changes in perception and mood
  • Auditory and visual hallucinations
  • Feelings of euphoria or deep awareness

However, caution is advised, as LSA can have a powerful effect on individuals. It is recommended to thoroughly research and understand the effects of LSA before use, especially for those new to the substance. Safety should always come first.

Safe use of LSA also involves understanding personal tolerance, and it is always important to maintain a healthy and informed approach.

Growing and caring for Hawaiian rose

Growing Hawaiian rose, also known as Argyreia Nervosa, can be rewarding. This plant is rewarding if it has the right conditions.

It needs full sun and well-drained soil to grow successfully. These conditions mimic its natural environment, which is key to healthy growth.

How to grow Hawaiian rose:

  • Choose a sunny location
  • Use well-drained soil
  • Water regularly, but don’t overwater

The plant can grow quickly, sometimes up to 10 meters tall if space allows. It thrives best in tropical to subtropical conditions.

The Hawaiian rose is also suitable for trellises or fences due to its ability to spread. It is easy to maintain if regular watering and sufficient sunlight are ensured.

New in our store: Argyreia Nervosa seeds and products

We have expanded our range with special Argyreia Nervosa products. For lovers of botanical rarities, we offer a fresh supply of seeds.

Our customers can thus enjoy not only the aesthetic beauty of the plant, but also its other benefits. Come and discover the magic of the Hawaiian rose!

How to use and store woodrose seeds correctly

Woodrose seeds have a variety of uses, but it is important to use them responsibly. They are commonly used for various purposes in the creation of teas or extracts.

Proper storage is key to maintaining the quality and effectiveness of the seeds. Make sure they are protected from moisture and light.

Storage tips:

  • Store seeds in a dry, cool place.
  • Use airtight containers for maximum protection.
  • Keep them out of the reach of children and pets.

Proper use and storage ensures that the seeds remain fresh and effective for a longer period of time.

Legal aspects and availability of LSA in the Czech Republic

The legal status of LSA is a complex issue. It is important to be aware of legal restrictions before purchasing or using seeds.

In some areas, sales or distribution may be regulated. Therefore, check local laws before purchasing.

Important factors:

  • Check local legislation regarding LSA.
  • Only purchase from trusted suppliers.
  • Be aware of potential legal risks.

Why choose Argyreia Nervosa?

Argyreia Nervosa offers a unique combination of beauty and practical uses. It is fascinating for gardeners and lovers of ethnobotanical plants. Its seeds contain LSA, which can contribute to personal growth and discovery. Choose this versatile plant for your garden, natural remedies, or studies.

title.rendered: 🌿 VivaDzen on Cannafest 2025!

content.rendered:
Dear VivaDzen customers, we are pleased to announce our participation in one of Europe’s largest trade fairs focused on cannabis and other natural products – Cannafest 2025. This prestigious event will take place in the heart of the Czech Republic, in Prague, and we are thrilled to be a part of it.

What is Cannafest 2025?

Cannafest is an international trade fair that attracts thousands of visitors from around the world every year, and 2025 will be no exception. We expect this event to bring together experts, enthusiasts, and entrepreneurs who share a passion for cannabis and natural products. The fair will offer a rich program full of lectures, workshops, and presentations of industry news.

VivaDzen at Cannafest 2025

At Cannafest 2025, we will present our latest products, including the popular kratom, which is in high demand among our customers in Prague. At our stand, you will have the opportunity to try different types of kratom and learn more about their effects and uses. Our experts will be happy to provide you with all the information you need and answer your questions.

Program and schedule

Cannafest 2025 will take place from November 7 to 9 in Prague. During these three days, you can look forward to a varied program that includes lectures by leading experts, workshops focused on innovation and new trends in the field of cannabis and natural products, and, of course, presentations by participants from around the world.

Program highlights

  • Lectures: Every day, there will be lectures on topics such as cannabis legislation, medical use of cannabis, and sustainable cultivation.
  • Workshops: Practical workshops where you can learn new skills, such as how to make cannabis products.
  • Networking: A great opportunity to make new contacts and share experiences with other participants.

How to join us?

If you want to attend Cannafest 2025 and visit our stand, we recommend purchasing tickets in advance, as high attendance is expected. For more information about the event, including a detailed program and registration options, visit the official Cannafest 2025 website.

We look forward to your visit and to sharing our passion for cannabis and natural products. VivaDzen looks forward to welcoming you to this exceptional event!

📅 When: November 7–9, 2025

📍 Where: PVA Expo Praha Letňany, Prague

title.rendered: Origin and export of kratom 2025 – Why country and batch matter: Indonesia vs Thailand

content.rendered:
Kratom, a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, has gained worldwide attention. Its leaves are known for their unique alkaloid profile. This profile varies depending on the country of origin.

Indonesia and Thailand are the main sources of kratom. Each of these countries offers different characteristics due to different growing conditions. Indonesia is currently the largest exporter with a robust supply chain.

Thailand, which recently legalized kratom, is becoming a strong competitor. This change opens up new opportunities for export. The quality of kratom can vary significantly between batches.

Factors such as soil quality and harvesting methods play a key role. Looking ahead to 2025, the kratom market is poised for change. These changes will be driven by changes in regulation and increased demand.

In the Czech Republic, kratom is growing in popularity. More and more consumers are looking to buy kratom in Prague and other cities. To make an informed purchase, it is essential to know the origin and quality of the batch.

This article discusses the future of kratom exports in 2025. It highlights the importance of country and batch quality and compares Indonesia and Thailand.

What is kratom and why is its origin important?

Kratom, botanically known as Mitragyna speciosa, is a tropical tree found primarily in Southeast Asia. The leaves of this tree have been used in traditional practices for centuries. People seek it out for its unique alkaloid composition, which has various effects.

The potency of kratom is influenced by several factors, including where it is grown. The climate and soil of each region contribute significantly to the chemical profile of the leaves. This results in a diverse range of effects and potencies that influence consumer choice.

Why origin matters

  1. Climatic conditions: The tropical climate is essential for the development of alkaloids.
  2. Soil composition: Nutrient-rich soils increase the potency of kratom.
  3. Harvesting techniques: Local practices influence quality.
  4. Cultural practices: Traditional knowledge influences cultivation methods.

Indonesia is a leader in kratom exports due to its established practices. It offers consistent quality and a wide variety of strains. Indonesian kratom is valued on the international market for its potency and reliability.

Thailand, which has a long tradition of kratom use, offers unique varieties known for their diverse effects. Since legalization, Thailand has reestablished itself as a key player in kratom production.

The history and present of kratom cultivation in Indonesia and Thailand

Kratom has a long history in Indonesia, where it has been cultivated for generations. The country is a world leader in kratom production. It has optimal conditions for cultivation thanks to its tropical climate and rich soils.

Indonesian farms often practice traditional methods that have been perfected over the years. These techniques ensure a stable supply of high-quality kratom to the global market. Kratom exports are a significant source of income for local communities.

In Thailand, on the other hand, the history of kratom has been influenced by legislation. Kratom was long outlawed, which limited its production and export. The situation has only recently changed, opening up new opportunities for Thai farmers.

Following the legalization of kratom in Thailand, many farms have begun to adapt to production and export. Thai kratom is valued for its mild but effective nature. Thailand is thus beginning to compete with Indonesia on the international stage.

Key differences between Indonesia and Thailand:

  • Legal conditions: Thailand has recently legalized kratom, while Indonesia has a long history of exporting it.
  • Agricultural methods: Indonesia relies on traditional techniques, while Thailand is adapting them to modern requirements.
  • Historical use: Kratom has deep roots in traditional medicine in Thailand.

Many Thai farmers are now focusing on improving the quality and diversity of their products. The goal is to compete with the established Indonesian market with unique Thai varieties.

The economic benefits of kratom are crucial for both countries. It provides jobs and supports local communities. With demand continuing to grow, both countries are expected to continue expanding their production capacities. The kratom industry can thus play an important role in their economic development.

Indonesian kratom is world-renowned for its diversity and availability. It is produced in different varieties that offer a wide range of effects. The dominant Indonesian kratom includes red, green, and white veins, each with specific properties.

Thai kratom, on the other hand, boasts strong and long-lasting effects. Varieties such as Maeng Da are popular among users for their effectiveness. Thai production is smaller but focuses on a specific high-quality target group.

Key differences in quality:

  • Drying process: Indonesia uses traditional methods that stabilize quality.
  • Thailand: Focuses on the premium segment and unique varieties.

Effects and consumer preferences:

  • Suitable for beginners and experienced users.
  • Thai kratom: Stronger and more intense effects.
  • Popular among demanding users.

Some users prefer Indonesian kratom for its availability and wide range of effects. Others choose Thai kratom for its strength and quality. The choice often depends on personal preferences and desired results.

Thai kratom is often praised for its consistency. Its standardized cultivation produces high-quality and reliable products. Indonesian kratom, on the other hand, is valued for its traditional and natural cultivation.

Price differences between Indonesian and Thai kratom also play a role. Thai kratom tends to be more expensive due to its limited availability and specialization. Indonesian kratom is generally more affordable, making it a popular choice for a wider range of consumers.

Choosing between Indonesian and Thai kratom can be challenging, but understanding these differences helps consumers make a decision. The final choice depends on individual needs, preferences, and expectations from kratom.

The Importance of Batch: How Does It Affect Kratom Quality?

The batch of kratom can significantly affect its quality and effectiveness. Different batches may come from different harvests, resulting in differences in composition and effect. Each harvest involves different growing conditions, which can affect the overall product.

Regular quality control is key to ensuring consistency in each batch. Certification and batch testing help maintain high standards. Without these steps, the quality of kratom can be highly variable.

Key factors affecting batches:

  • Soil conditions and climate
  • Harvesting and processing methods
  • Drying and storage time

Consumers often look for batches from certified suppliers. Certification guarantees that the batch has undergone thorough quality control. Customers can then be sure that they are getting high-quality kratom.

Knowing the batch is also important for tracking consistency of effects. Users who find a favorite batch can more easily repeat their experience. Suppliers often list the batch number, which helps track origin and quality.

Batches thus play a key role in the world of kratom. They are an important indicator of a product’s quality, effectiveness, and consistency. Thorough monitoring and understanding of batches is crucial for conscious and informed consumer decision-making.

The kratom export process in 2025: Legislation, certification, and trends

Kratom exports are undergoing dynamic changes. Legislation and certification play a key role in its international trade. As global demand increases, so do quality and safety standards.

Significant regulatory shifts are expected in 2025. These will affect the process of exporting kratom to major markets. The rules will focus on transparency and traceability of the supply chain. This will ensure that kratom is produced and processed ethically.

Key aspects of export legislation:

  • Mandatory quality certification
  • Compliance with international regulations

Certification is a necessary step for entering global markets. Certificates ensure that the product meets strict quality criteria. This gives consumers confidence in the safety of their purchase.

In addition, exporters must monitor current trends and demand. Requirements for the purity and consistency of kratom are constantly evolving. New technologies can bring innovations in processing and packaging. These factors can significantly affect competitiveness.

Trends in kratom exports:

  • Increasing emphasis on sustainability

Technological advances bring new opportunities to streamline the export process. For example, advanced drying and packaging methods can improve product shelf life. Sustainable practices are also gaining popularity among suppliers.

In 2025, these aspects will be crucial for successful kratom exports. Producers and traders will need to monitor developments and adapt quickly to changes. This will allow them to remain competitive and respond effectively to market demands.

The kratom market in the EU is constantly evolving. So it’s a great time to discover these natural options in your city.

Sustainability and environmental impacts of kratom cultivation

Kratom cultivation is associated with several environmental problems. If these are not addressed, there may be a negative impact on nature.

One of the main problems is deforestation. Kratom cultivation can lead to the removal of natural forests to create plantations.

Kratom crops should be planted with respect for the local ecosystem. Sustainable practices can help preserve biodiversity.

With growing demand, it is critical that farmers focus on:

  • Reforestation – restoring the original forest
  • Organic farming methods – without synthetic fertilizers and pesticides
  • Conservation of water resources – effective management and protection

Kratom farmers and producers are increasingly focusing on proven environmental practices. They are working with local communities and governments to protect the landscape and improve agriculture.

Consumers play a role in increasing demand for organically produced kratom. They demand transparency in the supply chain and prefer products from sustainable sources.

By 2025, sustainable agricultural practices could be the norm. This would ensure environmental protection and stable kratom production for future generations.

The Future of Kratom: Expected Market Changes by 2025

The kratom market is bound to change in the coming years. Technological and regulatory shifts are expected to affect its availability and quality.

Technology plays a key role in the cultivation and processing of kratom. Innovations increase efficiency and minimize environmental impact.

Regulation of the kratom market is likely to tighten. Transparency and adherence to standards will ensure that the quality of kratom is consistent.

Global demand for kratom is growing, motivating producers to improve quality and offer competitive prices. The market is becoming increasingly globalized.

Significant changes include:

  • Better certification standards – guaranteeing quality and safety
  • Increased government involvement – regulating exports and protecting consumers

Consumers will emphasize origin and freshness. Education and transparent marketing will provide greater confidence in available products.

The future of kratom is promising, but it requires the cooperation of all stakeholders. Open dialogue between farmers, governments, and consumers is key to sustainable growth.

Buying kratom is not just about price, but also about health value. A quality product is worth the investment.

Don’t forget about local regulations. Some areas may have restrictions on the sale or use of kratom.

Conclusion: Why the country of origin and batch of kratom matter in 2025

The origin and batch of kratom are key to understanding its quality and effects. These two criteria play a crucial role in the entire process, from cultivation to consumption.

The country of origin influences the alkaloid profile of kratom. Indian and Thai varieties have their own unique characteristics due to different climatic conditions and cultivation cultures.

In conclusion, kratom is not just about effects, but about responsible choice. Quality, origin, and batch are the three pillars that will shape the future of kratom on the market.

title.rendered: Kanna (Sceletium tortuosum) – African treasure

content.rendered:
It has been growing and helping people in South Africa for thousands of years… which is why it has earned the nickname „African helper.“ However, the modern world has only recently discovered its miraculous abilities. What makes kanna so special and how can it help you?

Kanna can grow in very harsh conditions

Kanna (Latin: Sceletium tortuosum) is a hardy medicinal plant from South Africa, where it has been growing for thousands of years and continues to grow today. Indigenous tribes in South Africa have relied on this herb since time immemorial. What has changed during the time this herb has been growing in Africa? Mainly the fact that the whole world has learned about it. Its ability to relieve stress, calm anxiety, and generally improve mood is tailor-made for today’s hectic times. Who wouldn’t want to feel better in today’s chaotic times? The herb, which today mainly comes in the form of capsules, powder, or tea, is unique in that, unlike other available stimulants, it is not addictive.

In South Africa, Kanna grows in very harsh conditions. It is a succulent plant that blooms with light yellow flowers. It has small fleshy leaves and survives in places where other plants are sure to die. Its superpower is to take care of itself, for example, by sacrificing older leaves. When the drought is so severe that even this plant cannot survive, its older, larger leaves dry up on the younger, smaller ones, providing them with shade and protecting them from the destructive rays of the sun. It is a true helper because, although it needs its strength itself, it can pass it on to those who use it. Indigenous tribes in southern Africa have always turned to this herb when they needed it.

Use by indigenous tribes

You may think that this plant, which reduces stress and anxiety, had little effect on indigenous tribes. Of course, they did not know the stress we know today. But that does not mean that their time was not stressful. The opposite is true. Hunters also experienced stress from hunting and the risk of being attacked and injured by animals. They were tormented by hunger and thirst. Indigenous tribes also lived in groups, and people had to maintain healthy social bonds within their tribe. They used the herb for various bonding rituals, tribal meetings, to relieve tension, and to improve communication.

They most often used the herb by chewing it like gum. In fact, Kanna can be translated as „something to chew“ according to their language. The fact that the indigenous tribes of South Africa were always chewing something was discovered in 1662 by a traveler and explorer who brought back exotic fruits and plants from his travels. However, the natives also smoked, dried, and fermented the plant, using it similarly to snuff. They used it not only internally but also externally. The herb became one of the most commonly used plants, literally the queen of their traditional medicine. They used it:

– for illnesses (where they utilized its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties),

– it worked great for toothaches,

– for stomachaches,

– it accelerated wound healing,

– the herb increased the endurance of hunters,

– overall, the herb helped them survive harsh conditions.

Nebyly nalezeny žádné výsledky.

What is the history of the kanna?

The African herb kanna carries with it the wisdom of thousands of years. The first mentions of its effects were discovered as early as 1685, when a 435-year-old drawing by botanist Simon van der Stel was found. Next to the drawing of the plant was a description stating that it was a creeping and perennial plant. Another early reference to this plant was a preserved record from 1662, which mentioned that Dutch merchant Jan van Riebeeck obtained this plant from indigenous tribes in exchange for goats. These references to the superpowers of this herb did not fade away. On the contrary, they gradually spread throughout the world. When the plant arrived in Europe, people described it as an herb similar to ginseng. Once the active ingredients were isolated from the plant, a series of studies began, which have continued to this day.

What substances does kanna contain?

What makes kanna capable of helping with illnesses, pain, and anxiety? Primarily, it is the cocktail of substances it contains. Among its most important substances are the alkaloids mesembrin, mesembrenone, and mesembrol. These substances:

– support cognitive functions,

– act on serotonin receptors and improve mood,

– have mild euphoric effects.

The plant also contains other valuable substances such as saponins, tannins, antioxidants, and so on.

What effects does kanna have on the human body?

Although kanna is used in traditional African medicine as a broad-spectrum remedy for a range of health problems, in our country, kanna is mainly discussed in connection with its ability to positively influence mood and alleviate stress and anxiety. Kanna:

– can eliminate stress, especially reducing its impact on our health, which in itself prevents a number of diseases caused by stress, such as:

– high blood pressure,

– diabetes,

– stomach ulcers.

Kanna:

– improves mood,

– relieves anxiety,

– strengthens mental resilience,

– relieves muscle tension (caused by stress),

– promotes sexual energy,

– can suppress thirst,

– can prevent overeating,

– promotes restful sleep,

– can be helpful in treating addiction (to cigarettes, alcohol, etc.),

– is not addictive in itself.

In what forms is kanna available today?

Kanna is available in various forms, most commonly as a powder (which has a weaker effect and is added to food or drinks, for example) or as a tea or extract (which is more concentrated and therefore has a stronger effect).

Who is kanna suitable for?

Thanks to its effects, kanna is suitable:

– for anyone who wants to lift their spirits and improve their mood,

– it is ideal for students and people in mental work, as it promotes concentration,

– it is suitable for people with anxiety and stress,

– kanna can help people struggling with addiction because it relieves withdrawal symptoms, reduces nervousness, and improves mental well-being,

– kanna can be tried by people who want to boost their creativity,

– The African plant can help people with stage fright because it breaks down communication barriers.

– For users who want to strengthen their resilience.

– For all those who prefer natural dietary supplements and do not want to burden their bodies with chemicals.

Is kanna safe?

This African helper is a safe herb when used in reasonable amounts and within the recommended dosage. However, the dosage is very individual. In general, beginners should start with a smaller dose. The dosage depends, of course, on the form of kanna used. The effects of kanna should be felt within about an hour of ingestion. Taking it on an empty stomach speeds up the onset of effects. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should at least consult their doctor before using kanna, as there are not yet sufficient studies to confirm its safety.

Kanna must not be used together with alcohol or antidepressants, as these substances may interact with each other and cause health complications. If you have taken more kanna than you can tolerate, you may experience:

– dizziness,

– headaches,

– general weakness,

– excessive sweating,

– rapid heartbeat.

In this case, it is necessary to stop using kanna or at least adjust its dosage.

It is no exaggeration to refer to kanna as an African treasure. The plant combines a long history with modern times, when its effects are highly sought after. What the inhabitants of South Africa have passed down from generation to generation is now being unraveled by numerous studies in an effort not to waste the medicinal potential of this plant. Dried powder from this plant is the most common form you can get. The plant is safe, and its main advantage is that it is not addictive. This makes it an ideal natural aid not only for low moods.

title.rendered: Corydalis Yanhusuo and its use in traditional Chinese medicine

content.rendered:
Corydalis Yanhusuo, also known as Chinese poppy, is a frequently used ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine. Why have people been interested in this plant for centuries, and what benefits does it offer?

Corydalis Yanhusuo and its botanical characteristics

Corydalis Yanhusuo is a perennial plant native to China, belonging to the poppy family. In nature, it grows to a height of 30 to 60 cm and has grayish-green leaves with pink to purple flowers that grow in clusters. However, the most important part of the Chinese poppy is its underground tubers. These are the main source of medicinal substances.

Corydalis Yanhusuo grows in the mountainous provinces of China, such as Sichuan. The tubers of the Chinese poppy contain several alkaloids, such as corydalis, dehydrocorydalis, and tetrahydropalmatine. All these alkaloids affect the human nervous system and act as effective analgesics. It is therefore no surprise that the first area of medicine in which Corydalis Yanhusuo found application was pain relief.

Other pharmacological effects

The analgesic effect of Chinese poppy has already been mentioned. It is even reported that Chinese poppy extracts can be as effective as morphine in pain relief. Unlike morphine, however, they do not create a risk of addiction. Corydalis Yanhusuo is therefore often used to relieve chronic pain caused by arthritis, migraines, back pain, menstrual pain, etc.

Extracts from the Corydalis Yanhusuo plant can also be used as a gentle sedative and help with insomnia or anxiety. The alkaloids contained in Chinese poppy also have anti-inflammatory effects. Traditional Chinese medicine uses virtually all of these properties and adds to them the support of blood circulation and the restoration of the body’s overall vitality. However, modern Western medicine and pharmacology are also slowly discovering the Corydalis Yanhusuo plant. Scientific studies confirm its very good analgesic properties and its effects in the treatment of depression and anxiety.

Modern medicine is even investigating its potential in the field of neuroprotection, with some studies suggesting that it could play a role in the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s. Only the future will tell to what extent this path can lead.

Nebyly nalezeny žádné výsledky.

Corydalis Yanhusuo and possible side effects

Unlike many other plants that we have inherited from ancient cultures, Corydalis Yanhusuo has the advantage of not posing any major risks. Nevertheless, it is important to ensure that extracts are used in accordance with the recommended dosage and to avoid violating certain basic rules. The main thing is that we should not combine this plant with any medications that also affect our nervous system. These are typically sedatives or antidepressants. Excessive consumption can then manifest itself in the form of dizziness, nausea, or excessive drowsiness.

Extracts from the Corydalis Yanhusuo plant should definitely not be consumed by pregnant women. There are two reasons for this. First, it can trigger menstruation and contractions, which in the worst case can lead to miscarriage. In addition, Corydalis Yanhusuo extracts contain certain alkaloids that are able to pass through the placenta and thus directly threaten the healthy development of the fetus.

Corydalis yanhusuo could also be dangerous during breastfeeding. It contains a chemical called berberine. Berberine can be transferred to infants through breast milk and can cause serious damage to the nervous system in newborns, including brain damage.

Another contraindication is a blood clotting disorder, which Corydalis yanhusuo can exacerbate. Extracts should therefore not be used after surgery.

Another problem is high bilirubin levels. Bilirubin is a chemical substance produced when old red blood cells break down. Under normal circumstances, it is removed by the liver. However, Corydalis yanhusuo also contains the aforementioned berberine, which can prevent the liver from removing bilirubin quickly enough. This can cause problems in people with high bilirubin levels.

Legal status of Corydalis Yanhusuo in different countries

In most countries around the world, Corydalis Yanhusuo is legal and freely available. Let’s start with its country of origin. In China and other Asian countries, the plant is widely available and often sold. It is most commonly sold as part of herbal mixtures, as an extract, or in the form of dried tubers.

In the European Union, it is also easy to buy Corydalis Yanhusuo in herbal product stores or online. The only restriction is that it cannot yet be promoted as a dietary supplement or even a medicine. This approach also applies to the Czech Republic. You can buy it in many places in Czechia. However, do not forget to consult your doctor. It is always worth it. The herb is also legal and commonly available in the United States and Canada. The authorities in these countries have not yet decided to classify it as a medicinal substance or a full-fledged dietary supplement.

However, there are also countries where Corydalis Yanhusuo is regulated or directly banned. This is the case, for example, in Australia, where Chinese poppy is only available on prescription, and a stricter regime also exists in some Arab countries and in Singapore.

Czech relatives of Chinese poppy

In the Czech Republic, the closest relatives of Chinese Corydalis Yanhusuo are the so-called dymnivky. The most common types are dymnivka dutá (Corydalis cava) and dymnivka plná (Corydalis fulva). They can be found in parks, deciduous groves, and private gardens. They were also used in folk medicine in the past. If you would like to grow some Corydalis, make sure you provide it with slightly acidic soil with a high humus content.

Growing Corydalis Yanhusuo

If you would like to grow this unique plant at home, you will need to provide it with soil that has even and, above all, constant moisture. It does not like dry or waterlogged soil. It is therefore ideal to water the plant once a week to maintain optimal moisture levels.

Corydalis Yanhusuo is impressively resistant to temperature fluctuations and can survive both sub-zero temperatures and heat up to around 38 degrees. However, this does not mean that it thrives in these conditions. During periods of extreme heat, it is therefore necessary to ensure sufficient water and, ideally, shade. In extreme frosts, mulching is recommended to help prevent root damage.

When growing, it is important to remove dead flowers and dead or damaged stems. This pruning is important to ensure optimal flowering and prevent the spread of disease. If you want to grow Chinese poppy from seeds, use fresh seeds and place them in well-drained soil with a light covering. In this case, too, it is necessary to maintain constant moisture without overwatering.

How to prepare Corydalis Yanhusuo for consumption

Corydalis Yanhusuo can be consumed in several ways. First, you can prepare a decoction. The dried tubers should be crushed or cut into small pieces and then boiled in water at a ratio of about 5 to 10 grams per 500 ml of water.

The second method is to prepare a tincture. This is done by steeping the crushed dried tubers in alcohol in a ratio of 1:5 for two to four weeks. Ten to twenty drops of this tincture can then be added to water or tea. Corydalis Yanhusuo can also be consumed in the form of ground dried tubers, which can be added to smoothies, for example. Of course, commercial products containing Corydalis Yanhusuo in capsule form are also available.

Corydalis Yanhusuo, or Chinese poppy, is an interesting plant that has been used in traditional Chinese medicine for hundreds of years to treat a variety of ailments. These include insomnia and chronic pain. Corydalis Yanhusuo is completely legal and freely available in most countries. This also applies to the Czech Republic. Nevertheless, it is advisable to follow certain rules when consuming it and to take into account any contraindications.

Conclusion

Corydalis Yanhusuo is a herb widely used in traditional Chinese medicine, primarily for its analgesic and sedative effects. Currently, it is also increasingly used in the West as a natural pain reliever that works similarly to classic analgesics. It helps with menstrual pain, muscle and joint pain, migraines, and neuropathic pain.

In addition, it has mild sedative effects and promotes sleep, making it suitable for insomnia and stress. It also promotes blood circulation, which can be beneficial for ischemic diseases or problems with cold extremities. In traditional Chinese medicine, it is often combined with other herbs and used to treat blood stasis, pain syndromes, and inflammation.

Although it has a number of beneficial effects, it should be used with caution, as excessive consumption can cause side effects such as drowsiness or a drop in blood pressure. It is also not advisable to combine it with certain medications, such as anticoagulants. It is always best to consult a doctor.

title.rendered: Kanna: Zlepšení nálady  Zvýšení koncentrace  Zvýšení energie 🌿

content.rendered:
Je čas zapomenout na únavu, napětí a neustálý stres. Představujeme vám Kanna (Sceletium tortuosum) – rostlinu, která harmonicky spojuje energii, klid a vnitřní rovnováhu.

🌱 Proč si vybrat Kanna?

– Energie bez výkyvů ⚡️: Dodává životní energii, která vás udrží v kondici po celý den, bez náhlých vzestupů a pádů.
– Klid a zmírnění stresu 🧘‍♂️: Jemně uklidňuje nervový systém a zanechává vás sebevědomým a vyrovnaným.
– Zlepšení nálady 😊: Zapomeňte na špatnou náladu – Kanna vám pomůže najít radost v jednoduchých věcech.
– Fokus a koncentrace 🎯: Snadněji se soustředíte na důležité úkoly a dosáhnete více za kratší čas.
– Přírodní složení 🌱: Žádná chemie, pouze síla přírody.

💡 Pro koho je vhodná?

– Pro ty, kteří chtějí být produktivní a vyrovnaní.
– Pro ty, kteří hledají přírodní podporu pro své tělo a mysl.
– Pro ty, kteří žijí v tempu moderního života.

👉 Objednejte si Kanna ještě dnes! 🌟

Objednat

title.rendered: Differences between Mitragyna Javanica, Mitragyna Hersuta, and Mitragyna Speciosa

content.rendered:
With some exaggeration, it can be said that Kratom has become a real „hit“ in the media and among politicians of all parties in recent years. The result is stricter regulation, but Kratom remains legal. Even so, many people are looking for alternatives. These include, for example, the Mitragyna Hirsuta and Mitragyna Javanica plants. Let’s take a closer look at them.

Comparison of three trees

Mitragyna Javanica, Mitragyna Hersuta, and Mitragyna Speciosa all belong to the same group. All three are native to Southeast Asia and were known to the indigenous people long before they were discovered by Western science and, more importantly, Western society. The leaves of all three contain alkaloids that can have both positive and negative effects on humans. However, they differ in one important respect.

In the West, as in Asia, people have come to love these trees because they can provide the body with energy when it needs it, relieve pain, and aid relaxation. However, as kratom, or Mitragyna Speciosa, gained popularity in our country and others, it also began to attract the attention of authorities, who focused on its negative aspects. In some countries, this has resulted in a complete ban on sales, while in others (such as ours) it has at least led to regulation. However, this applies to kratom; the other two trees have been spared so far. Why? Let’s take a closer look at all three trees.

Mitragyna Speciosa, aka kratom

Where else to start than with the most famous of the three trees mentioned in the title of this article? Mitragyna Speciosa, known as kratom, is a tropical evergreen tree that grows up to 30 meters tall. It is native to the rainforests of Southeast Asia, particularly Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. However, the most valuable part of the tree is its leaves, which contain a number of alkaloids with specific effects on humans. These are mainly mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine. These substances are responsible for its specific effects.

Kratom is most commonly used in the form of powder from dried leaves, which can be added to drinks, incorporated into food, or taken on its own. Just like the indigenous people centuries before us, people today value its stimulating and relaxing effects, which are used, for example, as an alternative to opioids in the treatment of chronic pain.

Přidat do košíku

In the Czech Republic, possession and use of kratom is currently legal, but its sale and distribution are subject to certain restrictions. These mainly concern the minimum age of the customer and the labeling of products containing kratom.

As with any other active substance, kratom has potentially positive effects, but also possible side effects. These may include increased blood pressure, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, etc. With weaker alternatives such as Mitragyna Javanica and Mitragyna Hersuta, the risk of these unwanted side effects is lower, which is one of the reasons why they are becoming increasingly popular.

Mitragyna Javanica

As with other plants and trees discussed in this text, Mitragyna Javanica (also known as Kra Thum Na) is native to Southeast Asia. As its name suggests, it is primarily found in the Indonesian islands of Java, Sumatra, and Borneo. However, it can also be found elsewhere. The tree grows up to 30 meters tall and is characterized by smooth, gray bark.

Mitragyna Javanica belongs to the same group of trees as kratom, Mitragyna Speciosa. Kra Thum Na has shiny, oval leaves with a smooth surface and gently wavy edges. It then blooms with small spherical flowers that are yellowish-green in color. Like kratom, this tree has been and continues to be used in Asian folk medicine.

Mitragyna Javanica leaves contain alkaloids that have mild stimulating and relaxing effects. Traditionally, Kra Thum Na leaves are dried and prepared as tea or chewed to boost energy and relieve stress and fatigue. Compared to kratom, however, Javanica is much milder. This makes it popular with people who are looking for a natural remedy to boost their energy or calm themselves down without wanting the effects to be too strong.

The alkaloid content of Javanica consists mainly of mitrajavynin, isomitrajavynin, and mitrajavin. Unlike kratom, it does not contain mitragynin and 7-hydroxymitragynin, which means that the effects of Javanica are slightly weaker. Mitragynia Javanica is not subject to any regulations and is completely legal in the Czech Republic.

Mitragyna Hirsuta

The second popular alternative to kratom is Mitragyna hirsuta, a tree also known by its Thai name „Kra Thum Khok.“ It also comes from Southeast Asia, specifically from Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, and Laos. However, the tree grows mainly in dry and rocky areas, which distinguishes it from other species of the Mitragyna genus, which prefer a more humid environment.

Mitragyna hirsuta is a medium-sized tree that commonly grows to a height of 15 meters. Its distinguishing feature is its oval leaves, which are dark green and, above all, have a finely hairy surface. This is such a typical feature of this plant that it is the source of its Latin name „hirsuta,“ which actually means „hairy.“ The tree’s flowers are small and yellow, arranged in spherical clusters.

Like kratom, the related tree Mitragyna hirsuta has been used in traditional Southeast Asian medicine for centuries. Indigenous people have known since time immemorial that the leaves of this tree have mild stimulating and relaxing effects, making them useful for managing stress, fatigue, or mild pain.

The leaves are traditionally dried and consumed in the form of tea, or chewed similarly to betel. Unlike kratom, which contains strong alkaloids such as the aforementioned mitragynine, Mitragyna hirsuta is milder and not as rich in alkaloids. Again, it is a milder and weaker variant. Mitragyna hirsuta is not subject to special regulation and is completely legal in Czechia.

Legal status of the three trees

The legal aspect of the matter has already been mentioned several times in the previous text. The whole situation can be summarized by saying that kratom is regulated in our country and banned in some other countries. In the Czech Republic, the need to protect children from kratom has been and continues to be emphasized.

As for the other two trees, Mitragyna Javanica and Mitragyna Hersuta, their alkaloid composition is slightly different and their effects are weaker. This is why they are currently protected from similar treatment in the vast majority of countries. Undoubtedly, this is also due to the fact that, unlike kratom, they are not yet as well known, and Western society has not yet begun to use and sell them on a large scale as it has kratom.

The question is whether, if kratom replaces them in terms of sales volume, a similar „process“ will occur with these trees and the products made from them. Either way, science should continue to pay attention to their properties and effects on human health, as research findings on their ability to have a positive effect on diseases such as Alzheimer’s suggest that it makes sense. Time will tell how the situation will develop. However, Mitragyna Javanica, Mitragyna Hersuta, and Mitragyna Speciosa have certainly not had their final say yet.

title.rendered: Ashwagandha – an adaptogen with a thousand-year history.

content.rendered:
Ashwagandha is a herb that has been around for thousands of years, but only now seems to have found its true potential. This is hardly surprising. Today’s hectic times, full of stressful factors, are crying out for it. Ashwagandha is a powerful adaptogen and therefore helps our body adapt to more complex conditions.

What is ashwagandha?

Ashwagandha (Latin name Withania somnifera) is an adaptogenic herb from India. It also grows abundantly in Asia, Africa, and other parts of the world where it has spread. You may know it as Indian ginseng. However, it has many other names, such as „winter cherry“ or „herb of youth.“ It has been a popular Ayurvedic herb for many years. The name ashwagandha – pronounced „ashwaganda“ – comes from the terms „ashwa“ = horse and „gandha“ = smell. The herb is said to have the strength of a horse and also smell like a horse. Symbolically, this name refers to its powerful effects and the specific odor of the plant’s roots. The herb is often associated with human strength, resilience, and endurance, as it promotes these qualities in people. It increases physical and mental performance and can also be used preventively.

What does the herb look like?

As it is a tropical plant, the herb is evergreen. It has oval leaves and is very attractive to look at. It is a robust perennial that grows to a height of 35 to 80 cm, depending on the conditions in which it grows. Ashwagandha blooms yellow-green, and after flowering, red berries appear, which are wrapped in a thin shell similar to a mulberry. Ashwagandha belongs to the nightshade family. Although it blooms and bears fruit, its most interesting part is undoubtedly its roots. These are narrow and grow to a length of half a meter to one meter. Nowadays, Withania somnifera can also be grown in our country. However, it will not survive frost outdoors. Therefore, it is necessary to grow the plant in a pot and store it indoors during the winter. However, this prevents the plant from developing a rich root system.

What is the history of this herb?

Ashwagandha has a history dating back 2,500 years. The first mentions of this herb can be found in ancient Indian medical texts called „Charaka Samhita“. Ashwagandha is an integral part of Ayurvedic medicine. Since ancient times, it has been used to strengthen the immune system, stimulate libido, and restore hormonal balance. A decoction of the root was an integral part of various ceremonies, rituals, and weddings… in short, occasions where it was necessary to strengthen both body and spirit. It is incredible that a herb thousands of years old is the ideal remedy for the vices of modern times – it helps the body respond better to stress and strain (the body then does not release as many stress hormones, which has a number of beneficial side effects).

Nebyly nalezeny žádné výsledky.

Which parts of the plant are used?

The most commonly used part of ashwagandha is definitely its long tuberous roots, which are dried and ground into powder. It is most often available as ground dried ashwagandha root or cut root (for preparing infusions). The powder is often processed into capsules, which are convenient to use. The root is therefore the strongest and most widely used part of the plant, but the leaves of ashwagandha can also be used, as they also contain medicinal substances, albeit to a lesser extent. Locals also use the berries of this robust herb. However, their use is not as common as that of the roots.

Main effect – powerful adaptogen

This herb is unique in that it belongs to a rare group of adaptogenic herbs. Herbs usually have a number of different effects, and emphasis is placed on those effects that predominate. In this case, all the spotlight is on the adaptogenic properties of ashwagandha. It helps the body by strengthening its ability to adapt to difficult conditions. Adaptogenic = increasing the body’s resistance to stressful situations (including stress, mental strain, and fatigue). Other adaptogens besides ashwagandha include ginseng, maca, basil, and so on.

What substances does ashwagandha contain?

The main substances in ashwagandha are called withanolides, which give the plant its main adaptogenic properties. These substances have been proven in studies to increase stress tolerance and protect against various pathogens.

Ashwagandha contains a number of valuable alkaloids, such as withanine, somniferine, withanine A, withanine B, and others. Other bioactive substances contained in this adaptogenic herb include flavonoids, glycosides, saponins, phenols, steroids, and steroid lactones. The herb also contains vitamin C, iron, and other minerals.

What does ashwagandha taste like?

If you expect the powerful properties of this herb to be accompanied by an exceptionally satisfying taste, ashwagandha will probably disappoint you. It tastes very bitter and its aroma is not particularly intoxicating. It is simply an effective herbal extract whose taste you will have to swallow or mix into something more palatable. That is why ashwagandha is added to yogurts, porridges, or smoothies, or consumed in the convenient form of capsules.

Rules of use

The recommended daily dose of ashwagandha varies depending on the manufacturer. The recommended amount is 250 to 600 mg per day, which will ensure anti-stress effects, improve sleep, and generally induce the desired effect. We always recommend following the recommended dosage indicated on the packaging. In order for the effects of ashwagandha to be noticeable, long-term use is necessary. The duration varies depending on the condition of the body. However, the minimum period of use is at least one month.

In what forms can you buy ashwagandha?

Nowadays, you can find ashwagandha in various forms – dried powder, cut root, capsules, tablets, tinctures, and liquid extracts.

Who can benefit from ashwagandha?

Given that ashwagandha has significant:

– anti-inflammatory,

– antioxidant,

– detoxifying,

– tonic,

– aphrodisiac,

– stimulating,

– diuretic,

– astringent,

– and antiparasitic effects, the range of people who could benefit from this herb is very wide.

The herb can be used by:

– people who are under stress, have a demanding job, or are going through a difficult period,

– people who regularly have to perform physically and mentally demanding tasks,

– people who experience anxiety (the herb calms anxiety and restlessness),

– athletes (ashwagandha promotes muscle growth and strength and accelerates regeneration),

– people with persistent fatigue (the herb has a positive effect on energy levels),

– people who want to have a baby (ashwagandha strengthens the reproductive system of both men and women),

– people who want to support their mental health, as ashwagandha is known to support memory and cognitive function,

– those who have trouble falling asleep and whose sleep is not of good quality,

– diabetics (ashwagandha stabilizes blood sugar levels),

– people who want to lose weight,

– people with heart problems (ashwagandha lowers blood cholesterol, regulates blood pressure, and strengthens blood vessels),

– women in menopause (the herb helps with the main symptoms of menopause),

– people who want to slow down the aging process in the body (the herb is known to promote vitality and combat the signs of aging).

What else can ashwagandha do?

The herb is known to:

– combat neurodegenerative diseases (it can therefore help with Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and so on),

– can help treat or prevent cancer,

– can help treat arthritis (thanks to its anti-inflammatory properties),

– significantly supports the immune system.

Can the herb pose a risk?

In normal doses, ashwagandha is completely harmless and its consumption is always beneficial. Any health problems may arise from taking higher doses or long-term higher dosages. Sensitive individuals may experience:

– skin rash, itching, and other allergic reactions,

– digestive problems such as diarrhea or vomiting,

– emotional numbness or sleep problems (the herb acts as a stimulant),

– in some cases, the herb may interact with thyroid medications, diabetes medications, or sedatives.

The herb is not intended for children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, or people with hormonal and autoimmune diseases.

How to recognize high-quality ashwagandha?

When choosing, it is necessary to consider several important points. These include:

– the amount of active ingredients (the higher the percentage of withanolides listed on the packaging, the better),

– purity of composition (the product should have either a minimum of additives or, preferably, none at all),

– price,

– verified manufacturer.

title.rendered: CBD drops

content.rendered:
CBD oils are gaining popularity among people who are dealing with a variety of health issues. They offer a natural way to relieve pain and have other health benefits. They are also very easy to use.

What is the history of CBD oil production?

CBD seems to be a recent phenomenon. In fact, however, cannabidiol is an integral part of the cannabis plant, which humans have been growing and using since time immemorial. It was therefore only a matter of time before people delved deeper into its composition and brought out the best of it. This happened in 1940, when scientist Roger Adams first used the abbreviation CBD for cannabidiol isolated from cannabis. Along with it, he also isolated cannabinol – CBN – and hypothesized the existence of the psychoactive substance THC. However, it was not isolated until 24 years later – in 1964 by scientist Raphael Mechoulam. He was the one who defined the properties of CBD in more detail. It was Mechoulam’s discovery that led to the exploration of what was then a new and unknown receptor system, which was named the endocannabinoid system (ECS). Elucidation of this system in the body led to even greater fascination with cannabis. Perhaps this was because it turned out that cannabis contains a powerful phytocannabinoid activator, CB 1 R. However, further studies were needed. At the same time, numerous discussions arose about the possibility of legalizing cannabidiol.

It can be said that it was not until 2000 that cannabidiol became known to the wider public, and awareness of this substance spread further through discussions on the internet. In that year, the availability of CBD on the market was already much greater, and demand for CBD oils and capsules began to increase. However, for a long time, CBD as a whole, along with cannabis, was on the list of substances controlled by the state, similar to tobacco or alcohol. This changed in the US in 2018, when cannabidiol was declared a legal substance (not all states did so). Other countries then followed suit in legalizing CBD. The general condition was a THC content of less than 0.3%. The limits for the legality of CBD vary from country to country. In the Czech Republic, the THC limit has been set at 1% since 2021.

Nebyly nalezeny žádné výsledky.

What types are there?

CBD oils can be divided into three basic categories:

– FULL SPECTRUM CBD,

– BROAD SPEKTRUM,

– CBD IZOLATE.

Full-spectrum CBD oils

Full-spectrum CBD oils are characterized by a strong cannabis flavor because, in addition to CBD extract, they also contain all other cannabinoids and terpenes found in cannabis. These products have the strongest effects. Full-spectrum CBD products naturally contain THC, but only in small amounts that do not cause intoxication.

What are the advantages?

The advantage of full-spectrum CBD oils is their beneficial therapeutic effect. Users who are not concerned about the small amount of THC, which is usually less than 1% (mostly 0.3%), can enjoy the benefits of other substances present, which have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects and support the therapeutic effect of CBD.

Broad-spectrum CBD oils

Broad-spectrum CBD oils contain all the substances that occur naturally in the cannabis plant, but during production, they undergo filtration, which leaves only certain cannabinoids in increased amounts. THC is present in broad-spectrum CBD oils either in very small amounts or not at all. Broad-spectrum CBD oil contains high levels of CBD, CBN, CBG, and CBC.

What are the benefits?

This group is chosen by users who want to avoid THC content but still want to enjoy the benefits of other phytochemicals in combination with cannabidiol.

CBD isolate

These are CBD oils from which other substances naturally contained in cannabis have been removed through intensive filtration and purification in order to obtain only CBD extract with 0% THC content. This extract is usually supplied in powder form and then used for the production of CBD oils or supplied in the form of an oil-based tincture.

Advantages

The advantage of CBD isolate is that it has no taste or smell, which makes it easy to add to other products and suits users who do not like the taste of cannabis. Another advantage is the 100% certainty that the product contains no THC. It is used by users who undergo drug testing and are concerned that the use of other products could affect the results.

CBD oils without THC

THC, or tetrahydrocannabinol, is a psychoactive substance in cannabis that causes a feeling of intoxication. While you may find small trace amounts of THC in full-spectrum and broad-spectrum CBD oils (which almost never cause intoxication or affect drug test results), CBD isolate contains no THC at all, nor does it contain any other cannabinoids. It is simply a CBD extract that may be preferred by highly sensitive users, users who do not want to consume even trace amounts of THC, or users who decide to do so for any other reason.

How to use CBD oils?

You can use CBD oils in several ways:

– place a few drops under your tongue and hold for about 1 minute before swallowing the oil (this is the most common method, which ensures rapid absorption),

– add to food or drink (this masks the unpleasant smell and taste for some people),

– take CBD extract in capsule form (a more convenient option for some people),

– apply CBD oils to the skin for a local effect (for example, for joint pain or skin care),

– inhale CBD oils (through an electronic cigarette filled with CBD liquids or through a vaporizer of dried cannabis flowers).

Please note that only CBD products intended for this purpose should be inhaled. Regular CBD oils intended for internal consumption would be harmful when heated, as their carrier oil would also heat up along with the CBD extract.

How to choose a good quality CBD oil?

1. Check the list of ingredients

When purchasing, you need to have a clear overview of what ingredients your CBD oil contains. You should know how many milligrams of CBD are in one bottle and how much is in one drop. A quality product does not hide its ingredients; on the contrary, it is transparent.

2. Consider the concentration of CBD extract

The effect of using CBD oil depends on the concentration of the extract. There is CBD 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and sometimes even more. Here you can follow a simple rule – the higher the concentration, the fewer drops you will need to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. It is also true that while low-concentration CBD is more suitable for beginners, high-concentration CBD is more suitable for experienced users.

3. Look at how the CBD oil was produced

Different companies use different extraction methods. The poor-quality ones even use toxic solvents such as hexane, pentane, propane, or butane for extraction. The ethanol method is considered the gentlest extraction method. This method extracts much more from the plant than the second gentle and high-quality method – CO2 extraction.

4. Find out where the cannabis was grown

This is also important because the plant absorbs contamination from the soil, which then leaves traces in the product. Give preference to products made from cannabis that has been grown without fertilizers and other contaminants.

5. Find out what the carrier oil is

The most commonly used carrier oils are MCT oil, hemp oil, olive oil (unlike other types, it may not be as stable), or avocado oil.

6. Buy only from verified and reputable manufacturers

7. Look at the price

A low price may be suspicious, because high-quality and environmentally friendly production comes at a cost.

Who can benefit from CBD oil?

– Users suffering from chronic pain (cannabidiol can relieve this),
– users with arthritis (cannabidiol has anti-inflammatory effects and relieves pain and the main symptoms of arthritis),
– People with multiple sclerosis (studies are still ongoing, but preliminary results show that cannabidiol may help suppress limiting symptoms),
– People suffering from anxiety and depression (CBD has a significant calming effect),
– people with epilepsy (cannabidiol helps treat certain types of epilepsy, which is why in 2018 the US Food and Drug Administration approved the use of CBD for the treatment of epilepsy – under the name Epidiolex. The drug is intended to treat seizures, specifically those caused by Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome),
– People with diabetes (some studies have shown that CBD can mitigate the effects of high blood sugar levels on cells, thereby also mitigating the frequent complications associated with diabetes).
– People addicted to opioids (CBD has been shown to reduce drug cravings, optimize heart function, and calm the nervous system).
– people with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) – CBD alleviates the symptoms of this disease,
– people who want to use CBD preventively (here they could take advantage of the high antioxidant effects of cannabidiol and prevent, for example, the development of Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, cerebral ischemia, or multiple sclerosis),
– People with post-traumatic stress disorder (CBD has a positive effect on treatment).
– People trying to lose weight (some studies suggest that cannabidiol helps break down fat cells).

title.rendered: The African plant Akuamma impresses with its effects

content.rendered:
Akuamma is another gift of nature with interesting effects on the body. The main role is played by the alkaloid akuammin found in the seeds of the Picralima nitida tree, which affects brain receptors and provides temporary relief from stress, pain, and tension. The substance is legal, but its dosage must not be exaggerated.

What kind of plant is it?

Akuamma is a shrubby tree native to West Africa. Akuamma refers to its main product – powder from the seeds of its fruit. The tree’s official name is Picralima nitida. It grows mainly around the rivers of West Africa, where it gets the moisture it needs. You will find it in Ghana, Cameroon, Congo, and Ivory Coast. It is a typical rainforest plant in West Africa with health effects that are unusual for us. For indigenous tribes, the tree is a cradle of health and first aid for injuries and other health problems.

The tree can grow up to 30 meters tall, but shorter trees are much more common. The Akuamma tree (Picralima nitida) blooms and bears fruit. Its fruits resemble coconuts. When opened, you will find pods full of seeds that are similar to pumpkin seeds. Powder from these dried seeds is the most common use of this tree. The fruits are harvested and the seeds are dried. They are then ground into a fine powder. Before this method of processing, the indigenous people of Africa chewed the seeds to extract their active ingredients. In addition to the seeds, they also used the leaves, bark, and pulp of the tree’s fruit, which also contain medicinal substances. They made decoctions, poultices, and ointments from them. However, not to the same extent as with the seeds. The seeds are the main part of this miraculous tree that is used.

History of its use

For people living in areas where Picralima nitida grows, this tree is like a green pharmacy. People have been coming to this tree for help since time immemorial. The seeds of the fruit were used primarily:

– as a remedy for dysentery (which can be fatal to local residents),

– to suppress the symptoms of malaria,

– to relieve fatigue,

– to reduce fever,

– for intestinal problems,

– to relieve pain.

Akuamma extract was used internally, but also externally in the form of a paste applied to wounds (for disinfection and better healing). Akuamma has anti-inflammatory properties. Indigenous tribes also used the tree in other ways, for example, its wood was used to make hunting equipment.

How is akuamma used today?

Today, akuamma is known as a powder for stimulation, invigoration, and mood enhancement. The alkaloids contained in the plant bind to opioid receptors in the brain, thereby exerting their effect. In addition to the above-mentioned effects, akuamma can also relieve pain and has a number of other scientifically proven effects. Although studies on akuamma extract are still ongoing, one thing is certain. Akuamma powder is very similar to kratom.

Nebyly nalezeny žádné výsledky.

What does akuamma powder taste like?

The powder has a bitter taste, so many people mix it into food or drinks to neutralize it. Capsules containing pure extract are easier to consume.

In what forms is it available as a product?

Today, akuamma seed extract can be purchased in powder form, which can be added to food or drinks. Capsules filled with this extract are also available, offering easier use.

Differences and similarities between akuamma extract and kratom

The powder from the seeds of the Picralima nitida tree, also known as akuamma, has many similarities with kratom powder from the Mitragyna speciosa tree. However, there are also a number of differences. What are they?

– The tree from which akuamma extract is obtained grows in West Africa, while kratom is obtained from a tree that is native to Southeast Asia.

– Akuamma is a powder obtained from the seeds by drying and grinding them, while kratom is a powder obtained from dried crushed leaves.

– Kratom is currently much better known than akuamma.

– Both substances have a very similar history of use by indigenous tribes for a range of health problems. In both cases, the indigenous tribes first chewed the seeds (akuamma) and leaves (kratom) to obtain the medicinal substances before moving on to more effective processing methods.

– Both substances work on the same principle, whereby the alkaloids they contain bind to opioid receptors in the brain (however, akuamma and kratom contain different alkaloid compositions).

What substances does akuamma contain?

The most effective substance in the akuamma plant is an alkaloid called akuammin, which plays a major role in the plant’s effects on the body. The plant also contains other alkaloids, such as akuammidine, akuammicine, pericine, alstonine, and others. In addition, the plant (especially its seeds) contains flavonoids, tannins, polyphenols, proteins, terpenoids, steroids, glycosides, carbohydrates, fats, and minerals such as potassium, sodium, iron, and zinc.

What are the most common effects of the plant on the body?

The main effects of the plant, verified by numerous studies, include the following:

– analgesic,

– antipyretic,

– antidiabetic,

– antimalarial,

– spasmolytic (relieves intestinal spasms).

Specific health effects of akuamma extract

– The effects are highly subjective and vary from user to user,

– positively affects energy levels,

– can improve mood,

– provides temporary relief from minor pain,

– relieves stress and anxiety,

– induces a better mood,

– provides a feeling of relaxation,

– lowers blood pressure,

– acts against cramps,

– stops diarrhea,

– improves sleep,

– has anti-inflammatory effects,

– may reduce stomach acidity,

– may treat stomach ulcers.

Caution: pregnant women should not use it, as some studies suggest that akuamma powder has adverse effects on fetal development. Akuamma extract is also not intended for children.

Who can benefit from this plant?

– Because the plant acts as a very powerful relaxant and relieves stress, its extract is useful for people who do heavy physical and mental work, people under stress, and people who need to relax.

– The extract from the Picralima nitida plant can be tried by people who have trouble falling asleep and are light sleepers, as akuamma can improve their sleep.

– Long-term use can increase libido, so it can be used by those who are dealing with problems in this area.

– Akuamma can help with quitting smoking and other addictive substances (it acts on the brain’s opioid receptors and can alleviate withdrawal symptoms).

Where can it be purchased in the Czech Republic?

Akuamma powder can be purchased in specialized stores and online shops.

Brief summary

The Akuamma plant is another in a series of plants that have miraculous effects on the body. What indigenous tribes have used in their traditional medicine since time immemorial is now being discovered by modern society. Studies are still ongoing. However, a number of positive effects on human health are already known. The most common description of this substance so far is that it is a relaxant that relieves stress and induces a feeling of well-being. However, in time, we may find that this substance plays a major role in the treatment of difficult-to-treat diseases. Nature created it for a reason, so let’s wait and see.

title.rendered: How to buy high-quality kratom and how to recognize a good seller

content.rendered:
It is, of course, legal to buy kratom in most EU countries. However, as with other products, you need to be careful about what you are buying and from whom. What should you pay attention to?

What types of kratom are available

Kratom is a product made from the leaves of the Mitragyna speciosa plant, a tropical tree that is used in traditional medicine in its native country. There are different types, which are primarily identified by color:

You can buy:

  • white kratom
  • red kratom
  • green kratom
  • brown kratom
  • yellow kratom
  • gold kratom

First, you need to familiarize yourself with the different types of kratom. They may be essentially equal in quality, but before buying, it is essential to know what type of kratom you are dealing with and what it is primarily intended for. The individual types differ from each other in the way they are processed, but also in their effects.

Red kratom

At harvest time, the leaves have characteristic red veins, which indicate full ripeness. In this case, they are left to ferment anaerobically for about 7 days during production and only then are they dried. Red kratom contains high levels of an alkaloid called 7-hydroxymitragynine. This gives it a mildly sedative effect and makes it suitable for general relaxation, better sleep, or pain relief.

Green kratom

In this case, the green veins indicate that the kratom is still ripening. The leaves are dried in the sun for one day, then the drying process continues indoors. Green kratom is somewhere between white and red kratom, thanks to its balanced ratio of active ingredients. It has a mildly stimulating effect, but also has a relaxing effect. It can induce mild euphoria, especially in higher doses. It can also be recommended for beginners and is suitable for long-term use.

White kratom

The leaves have white veins at the time of harvest, so the ripening stage is still early. With white kratom, drying the leaves in the sun should take more than a day. After that, they are dried in a closed space. White kratom has a stronger stimulating effect. It is therefore used for its ability to improve mood, increase energy, and enhance alertness. It strengthens concentration and performance.

The above-mentioned types can be considered basic. Yellow or gold kratom is not a separate type, but is created by mixing red kratom with white or green in various proportions. If you intend to buy brown kratom in the EU, you should know that even in this case, it is not a separate product. It is based on red kratom, which undergoes a longer fermentation process. This usually takes about 10 days.

How to recognize quality kratom

The choice of kratom depends primarily on individual preferences and previous experience. However, specific products may also differ in quality.

The most important factors to consider when purchasing high-quality kratom are:

  • country of origin
  • processing method
  • active ingredient content
  • product storage
  • verified manufacturer

Country of origin

A reliable manufacturer should first and foremost state where the kratom they supply comes from. The Mitragyna speciosa plant is native to Southeast Asia. High-quality kratom therefore comes from countries such as Thailand, Indonesia, and Malaysia. These areas are characterized by the best climate and soil conditions, which have a favorable effect on plant growth.

Kratom is usually labeled according to its color, but also according to the place where it was grown. For example, you can commonly find red Borneo kratom, which gets its name from the island of Borneo, the largest island in the Greater Sunda Islands.

Processing procedure

Harvesting usually takes place when the trees are 2 to 3 years old. Older trees provide higher quality leaves. However, the location where the tree grew also plays a role in this aspect, as plants in the outer parts of the plantation tend to have better access to nutrients. Nevertheless, the final quality of kratom is also significantly influenced by the processing of the raw material.

The starting form for kratom processing is always dried. The dried leaves are then ground into powder, which is used as tea or sold in the form of capsules or extracts. Drying and subsequent grinding should be carried out in such a way as to prevent the loss of active substances and contamination with foreign substances. Heavy metals and pesticides are particularly problematic in this regard.

Active ingredient content

The main active ingredients in kratom are indole alkaloids, particularly mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine. A trustworthy supplier is able to accurately declare what goods they are selling. Therefore, not only the purity but also the content of alkaloids, which are the main active ingredients, is verified by laboratory tests.

The total alkaloid content in one kratom leaf ranges from 0.5 to 1.5% by weight of dry matter. Of this amount, 60% is mitragynine and 2% is 7-hydroxymitragynine. Kratom varieties labeled as „Super“ are particularly high in active ingredients. These come from the leaves of mature trees, which are found at the tops of the plant.

Product storage

It is also advisable to choose fresh kratom. It has stronger effects and is less susceptible to mold or other contaminants. The packaging date should always be indicated on the kratom packaging. It should be stored in a dry and cool place.

If you are unsure, sensory evaluation can tell you a lot. It is therefore best not to buy kratom from unknown sources on the internet, but to have the opportunity to inspect it in person. Check that the product has the color and smell corresponding to its type. Any visual signs of mold are, of course, a sure sign that the seller has underestimated storage.

Verified manufacturer

It is also advisable to buy kratom from verified suppliers. These entities should not only be as transparent as possible about the information they provide about their products, but also have satisfied customers. If you cannot rely on personal recommendations, which is always optimal, at least check the reviews available on the internet.

A quality kratom seller also cares about customer convenience. They should therefore allow you to make a personal purchase in a brick-and-mortar store, but also place an order via their e-shop. Kratom delivery is also an option.
